I give up. The statement is false as written, so it can't be proved.

Take `f = Polynomial.C 2`. This is irreducible in `ℤ[X]`, because the constant 2 is a prime element of `ℤ`. For every prime `p`, the image of `f` in `(ZMod p)[X]` is either a nonzero constant or the zero polynomial. Neither has any roots in `rootSet`, so `n_p = 0` for every `p`. The numerator is therefore 0 for all `s > 1`. The denominator is positive for `s > 1`, so the ratio is 0 there. This makes `rightLim … 1 = 0`, not 1.

The intended statement presumably needs `f` to be non-constant, and that hypothesis is missing. Even with it, the proof would need the prime ideal theorem or Dedekind density, which is far beyond what I could do here.
